title: Build a Contact Form with HTML5 Validation & CSS States
description: Create a professional contact form with HTML5 validation attributes and CSS styling for all input states
objective: Students will build a contact form with proper HTML5 validation (required, pattern, minlength), style all input states (default, focus, error, disabled), and test accessibility

steps.title: Create the Form HTML
steps.instructions:
Create a new project folder with `index.html` and `style.css`. Build the form: ```html

Get in Touch

Have a question? We'd love to hear from you.

Please enter your full name
Please enter a valid email address
Enter a valid 10-digit Indian mobile number
Please enter at least 10 characters
``` Note the HTML5 attributes: `required`, `type="email"`, `pattern`, `minlength`, `maxlength`.

steps.title: Style the Default State
Add Interactive States
Style the Button
Test All Validation Scenarios
steps.instructions:
Remove `novalidate` from the form tag to enable browser validation.

Test each scenario and screenshot:

| Test | Expected Result |
|------|----------------|
| Submit empty form | Browser shows "Please fill out this field" on first required input |
| Type "abc" in email | Red border + error message |
| Type valid email | Green border |
| Type 1 character in name | Red border (minlength=2) |
| Type phone starting with 3 | Red border (pattern requires 6-9 start) |
| Type valid 10-digit phone | Green border |
| Type 5 chars in message | Red border (minlength=10) |
| All fields valid → submit | Form submits (page refreshes to #) |

Also test:
- Tab through all fields (keyboard navigation should work)
- Labels should be clickable (clicking label focuses the input)
- Placeholder text disappears when you start typing

**Submit:** The `index.html` and `style.css` files + screenshots of all 3 states (default, error, valid).

expected_output: A styled contact form with HTML5 validation showing three visual states — default (gray border), focused (purple glow), error (red border + message), and valid (green border) — working across desktop and mobile
